newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth to sell stake in overseas company. [CORRECTED 17:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BellSouth to sell stake in overseas company. [CORRECTED 17:30 GMT]

text.p: BellSouth Corp. said Tuesday it agreed to sell its 24.5 percent stake in Australia's Optus Communications Pty Ltd to Britain's Cable and Wireles Plc for $735 million.
BellSouth, the Atlanta-based telecommunications giant, said it expects to post an extraordinary gain in the third quarter ending Sept. 30 as a result of the Optus sale.
It also said Cable & Wireless will transfer to BellSouth its 22.3 percent interest in Colombian cellular company Occidente y Caribe Celular SA. This agreement is subject to government approvals.
(Corrects to show BellSouth receiving Occidente stake from Cable & Wireless, not selling stake to Cable & Wireless).
"We will reflect a gain in the third quarter, assuming the deal closes in the third quarter," a spokesman said.
"We don't know the magnitude of the gain yet because of taxes and the fact that it is an international transaction."

The spokesman added that Cable and Wireless will own 49 percent of Optus when the deal is closed. Australia's Mayne Nickless Ltd will own 25 percent and Australian institutional investors the remaining 26 percent.
BellSouth's stock rose 37.5 cents to $46.75 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
